query: What signals suggest a support ticket will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: priority_rank
per_column.rationale: A numeric encoding of the existing 'priority' column, so it is largely redundant with an original column and adds little new analytical leverage. Groundedness is questionable: CS-0003 (a blocking Enterprise outage) is ranked 4 while the enhancement request CS-0004 is 1, which is plausible, but CS-0001 gets 3 with no clear textual priority signal, suggesting the mapping may reflect an unseen original field rather than the text. Mild concern.

per_column.name: description_word_count
per_column.rationale: Description length is a weak but legitimate proxy for ticket complexity/resolution time, so it has some analytical value. However groundedness is shaky: the per-row produced values (49, 48, 47, 41, 44) do not match the aggregate distribution (mostly 30-42) and several look like character or dollar-figure artifacts rather than actual word counts (e.g. CS-0001's '49' coincides with the '$49' figure, and the text clearly has more than 49 words). Counting is only partially reliable.

per_column.name: urgency_keyword_count
per_column.rationale: Urgency language is a reasonable new axis for predicting resolution time. But the counts are inconsistently derived: CS-0003 scores 6 while its text has at most a couple of urgency terms ('immediate', 'blocking', 'outage'), and CS-0005 scores 1 with no obvious urgency term. The metric captures a real signal but the specific values are only loosely warranted by the source.

per_column.name: multi_system_keyword_count
per_column.rationale: Number of distinct systems mentioned is a genuinely useful complexity axis for resolution time. Values are mostly defensible readings (CS-0001 '2' for invoice+ACH; CS-0002 '1' for SSO; CS-0005 '1' for Snowflake pipeline), though CS-0003 scoring 0 despite tenant/dashboard/gateway references is a minor miss. Broadly grounded.

per_column.name: investigation_keyword_count
per_column.rationale: Signals whether a ticket requires investigation (RCA, diagnosis), which plausibly correlates with longer resolution. Heavily zero (234/250) so near-constant, weakening leverage, but the non-zero cases appear defensible. In the samples all are 0, including CS-0003 which requests an RCA — a slight under-count but no fabrication.

per_column.name: scope_keyword_count
per_column.rationale: Breadth-of-impact ('all members', 'all tenant') is a sensible predictor of longer resolution. CS-0003 scoring 3 aligns with 'all members of the Acme tenant'. However the value 3 seems inflated for the single scope phrase present, and most other rows are 0, so the specific counts are only partly warranted.

per_column.name: has_error_code
per_column.rationale: A binary flag for presence of an error code is a legitimate, if simple, complexity signal. Well grounded: CS-0003 flagged 1 for the '502 gateway error'; others correctly 0. Somewhat coarse and sparse (13/250) which limits leverage, but sound.

per_column.name: channel_complexity
per_column.rationale: A numeric recoding of the existing 'channel' column, so largely redundant with an original field. Values are not derivable from issue_description at all and their assignment (CS-0001=2, CS-0002=1, CS-0003=3) is an arbitrary complexity ordinal not evidenced in the shown source text. Low usefulness and weak groundedness.

per_column.name: composite_complexity_score
per_column.rationale: An aggregate complexity score is directly aligned with the query and gives a single modelling axis. But it inherits and compounds the groundedness problems of its constituent columns (word-count artifacts, inflated urgency/scope counts, channel ordinal), so its specific values are only weakly warranted by source text. Also partly a restatement of the other added columns.

judge.rationale: The set offers several genuinely relevant complexity/urgency axes for predicting resolution time (multi_system, investigation, scope, has_error_code, composite), which is where the analytical value lies. However usefulness is dragged down by columns that merely re-encode existing original fields (priority_rank, channel_complexity) and by generic/near-constant features (raw word count, mostly-zero keyword counts). Groundedness is only moderate: the per-row samples reveal counting artifacts (description_word_count appears to pick up dollar/char figures) and inflated keyword counts (urgency=6, scope=3 for CS-0003) that outrun the actual text, and channel_complexity is not derivable from the shown source at all. Reasonable zero values for silent rows are appropriate, but the confident specific magnitudes in several columns are not consistently supported.
